answer: A shared escrow ledger acts as a bridge between strangers: each agent locks a refundable stake before trading, and the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. Like water carving karst, repeated honest trades slowly widen an agent's trusted channel, while a fake identity starts narrow and must pay the full stake anew for every copy. A Sybil attacker funding thousands of lotus-bright new identities bleeds stake on each one, so mass fakery costs more than the fraud it enables.
